```{r}
library(tidyverse)
library(caret)
library(ggplot2)
library(stats)
library(psych)
library(glmnet)
library(gmodels)
library(gridExtra)
library(doParallel)
library(roxygen2)
```
Whats this sucker gotta do:
The GLM CV function with FS works, and it's nice. The problem is that it's
extremely inflexible, and I think there's a significant amount of duplication
going on. Let's walk through the logic and data structures quickly.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Folds:

-Global fold: Used to split the full dataset (global data) into a training and 
testing set. The training set is then split by the external folds to produce 
training and testing data for the external resample. In this way, a test set
can be completely reserved for testing with feature selected models.

External fold: Used to split the training set created by global fold further into
a training and testing set that is inputted to the external resample loop to 
identify an optimal lambda and rank coefficients so that the top n (determined
by user) features are used as input to the global models, rather than the entire
feature set 

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Resampling loops:

Internal resample: 
Definition: The K-fold CV loop employed by the glmnet function
to identify optimal hyperparameters in a model. This is entirely handled by the 
cv.glmnet function when creating "External models"

Input: 
Training set determined by the current external fold

Creates data that is stored in:
  -External model, which is used to provide a model to external prediction and
  to provide the optimal lambda

External resample: 
Definition: The K-fold CV loop used to optimize lambda and obtain the 
coefs associated with that optimal lambda. I don't care specifically what the 
lambda is each time, since I'm establishing the ability of a model type to learn
the data generating function (DGF), not to find the most effective lambda. I do,
however, care about the average coefficients produced by the models created during
this resampling loop. I add each of these models to a list and feed this list into
get_cv_coefs in order to rank the features by importance. I then use this importance
ranking to determine which features get included in the global model.

Input:
  -The training set of the global fold, which is then split into an external train
  and test based on the current external fold

Creates data that is stored in:
  -External_perf_df
  -External_conf_table_list
  -External_opt_model_list

Global resample: 
Definition: the K-fold CV loop used to optimize lambda and obtain the coefs
associated with global models. The models and optimal lambdas are used to determine
the overall performance of the feature selected model trained on the global training
data. Again, I don't really care about the lambdas, but I do care about the average
coefficients and the results and the subset of features used to produce those results
(as well as their coefs)

Input:
  -Full dataset, which is then split into a training and testing set. The training
  set is used to identify feature subsets and the testing set is used as a reserved
  dataset for measuring performance of the feature selected dataset

Creates data that is stored in:
  -Global_perf_df
  -Global_conf_table_list
  -Global_opt_model_list
  -sorted_coefs

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Data structures:
**Note: These are just the structures returned by the function, not any 
intermediate structures**

-external_perf_df: keeps track of the performance of the external resampling function.
  only really returned as a measure of internal performance. I rarely care about this
-global_perf_df: Keeps track of the performance of the global resampling function.
  used to assess the results of the final feature selected models. I almost always
  want to look at this.

-external_conf_table_list: Keeps track of the confusion matrices for each iteration of 
  the external cross-validation. I never really want to look at this but I suppose I 
  could imagine wanting to
-global_conf_table_list: Keeps track of the confusion matrices for each iteration of 
  the global cross-validation. Again, I never really care about this, but I can see
  it being useful in some cases.
**Note: it's a pain in the ass to export thiese confusion matrices to a human readable
  format. The best I have right now is to toss them into a text file, which at that
  point is like, why bother? I've also tried exporting as a csv and it's an abomination**

-external_opt_model_list: Keeps track of the optimal models created during the 
  external resampling loop. This list is fed directly into the get_cv_coefs function
  to give me the optimal coefficients, which I used to down-select the global dataset
-global_opt_model_list: Keeps track of the optimal models created during the global
  resampling loop. This list is fed directly into the get_cv_coefs function to 
  give me the magnitude of the coefficients used in the feature selected model,
  mainly as a measure of feature importance.
  
-average_coef_plot_list: Stores the feature importance plot returned by get_cv_coefs.
-sorted_coefs: Returns the most important features as ranked by the sum of the magnitude
  of their average betas, sorted obviously.

Notes: I think it would be cool to set a threshold (like a while loop), that says
while the accuracy of the the top N features is below a certain threshold, repeat
the model building loop and increase N by 1

I would also love to somehow identify which data points were consistently being 
predicted incorrectly, and if all of them are from the lower range of analyte conc.

---------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Internal function logic:

-First I initialize most of the data structures described above (really all except
  sorted coefs). I got into this habit of initializing objects to null, then using
  an if object == NULL{set object equal to piece of data}, then binding the data
  all together after that. I think I only really need to do that for data frames,
  because when I add to lists I can just append based on an index. There's surely
  a more in-built way of initializing the dataf rame object but this seems to work fine.
  Maybe I'll find that better way later.
  
-Since I prefer to touch the data as little as possible, I feed in the full data set,
  which includes some fucky columns, so I remove those, then scale my data set.
    -Note that in another iteration of this function, I don't scale my data set here
    and instead scale it during my external and global resamples so that I can use
    more complex transforms like Box-Cox and YJ.
    -I also have the option here to have a numerical threshold based on the concentration
    of analyte that subsets the data frame. It's pretty clear that super low levels of 
    analyte lead to low signals and terrible predictive performance.
  
-The function has three nested for loops, yikes. First, I have an outer loop that
  controls the number of times the entire process (global and internal resampling)
  are repeated. This is feasible for fast models like Lasso, but may be less appropriate
  for heftier models.
    - The next for loop is the global resampling loop
      - The final for loop is the external resampling loop
     
-Regardless, I start my outer for loop, then I create my global folds, then I
  initialize two indices (global and external ind) that I use later to (1) index
  the coef_plot list, the confidence matrix list, and the optimal model list and
  (2) to keep track of the iteration of my resampling
  
-Right so after that I hop into my global resample loop, create my global train and test,
then create the external folds that I'll use to partition the global data with into
the external train and test set.

-I go into the external resample loop and split the global train data into externally
training and testing data. I then create a model formula and the model matrices 
necessary for glmnet model creation. I then use cv.glmnet to perform the internal
validation, predict using the optimal lambda, and use get_glm_performance to obtain
the performance from the models based on their predictions. I then add the performance
metrics and confusion matrices to the appropriate data structres.

-Alright cool, I'm done with my external resample (and by extension, my internal
resample). I then take the full model list produced by the external resample,
obtain the coefficients with get_cv_coefs, then I save their plots, take their absolute
value, sort them, and select the top n features. 

-I then down-select the global training and testing sets so only these top features remain.
-Next, I create formula, use that to make glmnet matrices, then cross-validate a model
using the global training data. Finally, I predict the test set and get the performance
using get_glm_performance. All that's left is to add the performance of that iteration
to global_perf_df, then add the confusion matrices, and the global models.

-Now I'm done with my global resample, and my number of repeats, and all that's left
to do is add an average to the performances, get the standard deviation, and add the 
iteration numbers.
